messages:
ana: mid-morning check-in — quick status: yesterday I landed the kernel slot-fairness change (PR #487). ran microburst bench, saw p95 drop ~12% for short sequences but one canary node hit OOM when batch_size > 32 on long seqs. blocker: need a guard in the allocator to avoid oversized contiguous reservation. today: add guard, run a 3x bench sweep, and coordinate canary redeploy. cc @oncall :hourglass:

mike: saw the PR, left a comment about using atomic compare-and-swap for the guard. can you add a small unit test? also can you paste the repro logs so infra can triage? :eyes:

ana: sure, adding test now. repro log snippet below:
```
[2025-06-05T09:12:04Z] runtime: allocation failed: oom after 3.2GB reserved
stack: runtime/kernels.cc:442 allocate_slots
params: batch_size=64 seq_len=4096 model=redwood-13b-qat
```

sara: quick thought — this smells like KV cache eviction thrash when seq_len spikes. try running with `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.8` and smaller `CACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW`. if that stabilizes memory, we can add a safe default for canary. :thinking_face:

ana: good call. will try `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.8` and post results. @ryan can you eyeball the scheduler change in the PR? I touched slot allocation there.

ryan: on it, will review today. I also noticed a slight p95 regression in canary 2.3.4 -> 2.3.5: `p95: 121ms -> 138ms` on the microburst harness (seq=256, batch=16). maybe the new batching heuristic trades latency for throughput. leaving a comment with a repro command.

ci-bot: CI update — master build passed, canary build failed the oom-test (test/oom_repro). logs uploaded to CI artifacts.

mike: if canary fails the oom test, we should add an automatic fallback policy: if oom detected during warmup, cap batch_size to 16 and mark node unhealthy for 5m. filing INF ticket.

ana: created INF-322 and linked to PR #487. adding test and allocator guard now. timeline: bench by 11:30, patch ready by 14:00, canary redeploy ~17:00 PST. will post bench numbers here.

sara: for the bench runs, please use `bench-runner --repeat 5 --seq 512 --batch 32 --capture=latency.p95` and include raw JSON. I'll run a parallel sweep with evict threshold variations after lunch. :wrench:

ryan: small nit in PR — prefer `std::atomic` over a mutex for the hot path. otherwise lgtm. also we might consider a graceful degradation metric in console so ops can see fallback events.

ana: noted, switching to atomic. will also add a small metric `kernel.alloc.fallback_count`. will ping infra for canary repro access.

mike: thanks. ping me if the canary still noisy after the fallback policy — I can hotfix the autoscaler config. :thumbsup:

ana: will do. posting bench results in this thread when ready. thanks team! :rocket:
